name: Shower hood (hair protector)

lead:
A shower hood is a waterproof cover worn over the hair while bathing. It keeps hair dry so a styled look or a recently done treatment stays intact.
The appearance payoff is preserved hair styling and less washing frequency, with the cap also used to trap heat during masks or dye.

paras: It is pulled over the head, usually with an elastic edge, before showering. People also wear one during hair masks or dye so the cap holds in warmth.
No notable risks beyond comfort; cheap versions are plastic and reusable fabric ones are also sold.

angle.text: By keeping water off, a shower hood preserves a blow-out or set style and lets hair treatments work under trapped warmth.

lead: A shower hood, more commonly called a shower cap, is a waterproof hat worn while showering or bathing to protect hair from becoming wet.[1] Most have elastic edging, and some join two layers of fabric to be waterproof and decorative.[1]

People use it to keep a blow-dry or style from frizzing, and a cap also traps heat so a hair mask or dye can set; spas use them during facial masks.[1] Some versions for children have wide brims to keep shampoo out of the eyes.[1]
A claimed German origin around 1970 for a hood protecting hair and makeup could not be verified in published histories. No studies of shower caps exist.

paras: Shower caps range from single-layer waterproof material to two-layer fabric designs; plastic bags are often used as improvised caps.[1]
Protecting styled hair, helping masks or dye set with trapped heat, and spa facial treatments.[1]
